newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cultus discovers new gas in Otway Basin.
newsitem.headline: Cultus discovers new gas in Otway Basin.

text.p: Cultus Petroleum NL said on Wednesday it has discovered a new gas field in the Victorian section of the Otway Basin in Australia.

"The exploration wildcat well Fenton Creek 1 flowed gas on drill stem test (DST 2) at 160,900 cubic metres per day (six million cubic feet per day) accompanied by 6.9 cubic metres of condensate per day (43 barrels per day) from reservoir sands in the Late Cretaceous Waaree Sandstone over the interval 1574-1584 metres," Cultus said in a statement.
It said the test was run through a 12.7 mm surface choke.

"A previous test (DST 1) of the Early Cretaceous Eumeralla Formation over the interval 1699-1714 meters flowed gas to surface at a rate too small to measure through a 6.35 mm surface choke," Cultus said.
Cultus said Fenton Creek 1 reached a total depth of 1840 metres on April 4 and would be cased and suspended as a future gas producer.
Fenton Creek 1 is a Santos Group operated well in the petroleum exploration permit (number 108), onshore Otway Basin, Victoria. The licence is located 170 kilometres west south west of Melbourne.
At 12.20 p.m. (0020 GMT), Cultus shares were trading at NZ$3.20, up 30 cents.
